trust_decision.summary: Body text of a module output shortcode, which any Contributor can write into post content, is passed to PHP unserialize() with no class restriction and so is trusted as plain option data. The decision is made in each module's dslc_module_*_output shortcode handler.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the dslc_module_posts_output shortcode. Its handler is the function registered at modules/posts/module.php:6374, and it unserializes $content at line 5622.

fix_sites.entry_point: [dslc_module_posts_output] shortcode in any post content rendered on the front end (Contributor+ can author it)
DSLC_Posts::output(), the producer side: called when the posts module renders and emits the shortcode body (serialize changed to json_encode)
fix_sites.module_kind: serializer / producer in the module class

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches one module file only (fix.diff:166-234). The other commit (fix.diff:1-147) is an unrelated DOM XSS fix in JS.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names only the posts shortcode. The WooCommerce module is not registered (includes/functions.php:70 is commented out), yet its shortcode is still registered at load time (modules/woocommerce/module.php:5649 via includes/functions.php:700-711). A solver could argue it is a disabled or legacy module. The comments and comments-form handlers look like a separate 'tp-' (theme-part) feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing pages hold legacy PHP-serialized option arrays in the shortcode body, including strings whose length prefixes are broken and need the regex length fix-up. These must still render, so a fix that drops unserialize or rejects non-JSON content breaks saved pages.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The legacy base64+serialized branch of dslc_json_decode, with allowed_classes dropped on the base64 path only
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The commented-out lines at 1047 and 1051 show the maintainer already switching between restricted and unrestricted unserialize on this legacy path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Preset code decoded with maybe_unserialize(base64_decode(...)) on render (currently a commented-out line)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The commented line shows that this exact decode existed for legacy presets. Re-enabling it as a fallback for old presets is plausible.

O10_build.language: PHP (WordPress plugin; JS for the editor)

O10_build.project_tests: phpunit.xml points at tests/phpunit/ (phpunit.xml:2,11), but that directory is absent at the pinned commit. The only tests are Codeception browser acceptance tests (tests/acceptance/*Cest.php), and none cover shortcodes or deserialization.

j.j_sites_touched: modules/posts/module.php (security fix); ds-live-composer.php and readme.txt are version bumps; the JS files belong to the separate XSS commit
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add ['allowed_classes'=>false] to the posts handler only (missing the second unserialize in the length fix-up branch), or replace unserialize with json_decode and break existing serialized pages

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit 2b0b430 is a separate DOM-based stored XSS fix in pagination JS (fix.diff:1-147), which is not this advisory's protection.
Several maybe_unserialize calls on admin-controlled options (includes/ajax.php:547, includes/class.module.php:4744, includes/styling-presets.php:37) were not pursued.
